rationale: A is substantially more decision-useful because it compares concrete live options, quantifies expected accuracy/runtime tradeoffs, identifies when the recommendation would fail, and gives implementation triggers and review thresholds. B gives sensible general advice and a workable strategy, but it stays mostly qualitative, offers weaker discrimination among alternatives, and provides little uncertainty quantification or numeric support. For a careful human deciding parameter strategy under competing objectives, A better supports an actual choice rather than just a direction of travel.
